purpose: Booking Register Finance hospitality expense category/type seed master; not a substitute for a legal-entity-specific CA-approved chart of accounts
status: proposed defaults for user review; statutory mappings require CA validation

standards_referenced.name: ICAI Technical Guide on Audit in Hotel Industry (2011)

design_rules: Canonical codes are immutable; rename display labels only
Categories and types are seeded, not hardcoded into the expense entry screen
Visibility is per property; hidden types remain searchable to authorized users
Never delete used types; archive instead, preserving historical codes
Every expense carries legal entity, property, department, type, service period, gross amount, tax lines, vendor and payable/payment link
GST/TDS rules are separate, effective-dated, CA-configurable tax mappings; do not infer them from type alone
Payments, vendor advances, guest refunds, refundable deposits, loan principal and tax remittances are not expense types
Capital purchases, improvements and inventory movements use separate workflows
Accrual posting and cash settlement are distinct; no duplicate expense when paid
Default suggested classifications must be confirmed for ambiguous searches
Staff cannot create or remap accounting ledgers without approval
Statutory group and USALI departmental mapping are independent dimensions

accounting_approval_notes: Type-level statutory groups are indicative; a CA must validate against legal entity and applicable AS/Ind AS
Some food purchases are inventory, not immediate consumption; use inventory workflow when stock is tracked
Hotel leases may be recognized differently depending on accounting framework; the rent category is operational input, not automatic statutory expense
USALI 12th treats in-room TV/entertainment costs under Information & Telecommunications Systems; Indian ledger presentation may differ
Expense master is not a substitute for double-entry general ledger, inventory, fixed asset register, payroll or statutory tax ledgers
